target.title: Rework Android gateway onboarding setup
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves Android first-run gateway setup was hard to follow: the setup-code path was not clearly the recommended authenticated path, nearby discovery looked like a primary pairing method even though it only helps with endpoints, and the transition through connecting, node approval, and connected states gave users little guidance. ## Why This Change Was Made This reworks Android onboarding around the current product truth: generating a setup code with `openclaw qr` is the golden path because it carries bootstrap auth, nearby gateway discovery can only assist with an endpoint, and manual setup is a fallback. It also gives node approval and connection progress dedicated UI states so users know what is happening after a QR scan or setup-code entry. ## User Impact - New Android users see a dark-mode welcome screen, a clearer gateway connection choice screen, and a setup walkthrough before scanning. - The QR scanner opens inline in a square camera tile, with close, gallery, and setup-code fallback controls available from the same screen. - Manual setup stays available as a fallback, with local nearby endpoint data used as prefill when available instead of as a separate primary action. - Pairing progress now explains gateway check, secure session creation, and node approval waiting states; successful pairing lands on a connected screen before continuing. - Camera permission for QR scanning remains separate from granting OpenClaw camera tool access. ## What Changed - Android onboarding UI: replaces the old gateway pairing flow with welcome, connect gateway, setup gateway, inline scanner, setup-code, manual, progress, approval, error, and connected states. - Navigation behavior: centralizes expected back transitions for the onboarding subflow and covers them with logic tests. - Android gateway state: persists gateway auth/session details, distinguishes setup progress from node approval, and removes the inactive sign-out dead end from the paired shell path. - Bootstrap handoff: updates the device bootstrap contract/tests/docs for bounded operator handoff scopes used after mobile pairing. ## Screenshots Captured from the `OpenClaw_Pixel_8_API_35` Android emulator at 1080x2400. Full phone viewport is used because the changed header/back controls, vertical centering, scanner tile, and bottom actions are part of the proof. | Screenshot | Claim Proved | State | Viewport | Crop Choice | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | Welcome uses the dark-mode Android shell with concise setup expectations and one bottom CTA. | Fresh install / welcome | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Gateway choice screen makes setup code primary and manual setup secondary without promoting nearby discovery as pairing. | Connect Gateway | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Setup walkthrough explains starting the gateway and generating a setup code before scanner actions. | Setup Gateway instructions | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | QR camera opens inline in the scanner square and keeps close/gallery/setup-code controls in context. | QR scanner active | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Scanner tile has a readable camera-unavailable state with the same fallback actions. | QR scanner with no emulator camera | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Setup-code entry is reachable as a focused fallback instead of a confusing scanner input box. | Enter setup code | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Invalid setup code feedback is prominent and recoverable. | Invalid setup-code error | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Manual setup remains a fallback with URL/token fields and clear pairing action. | Manual setup | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Connection progress is contained inside the main setup box with explicit current work instead of a silent spinner. | Connecting progress | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | | | Later pairing progress/approval state keeps the user in setup with visible next-step progress. | Approval/progress state | 1080x2400 | full phone viewport | ## Verification - target.title: fix(message): thread --limit through to CLI formatter and surface provider pagination hints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #71452

`renderMessageList` in `src/commands/message-format.ts` hard-coded `messages.slice(0, 25)`, so `message read`, `message pins`, and `message search` always capped CLI table output at 25 rows regardless of `--limit`. Provider pagination signals (`hasMore`, `nextBatch`, `@odata.nextLink`) were silently discarded — users had no indication more results existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three gaps in the end-to-end data flow:

1. **Formatter cap**: `renderMessageList` did not accept a caller-provided limit, defaulting to a hardcoded 25.
2. **CLI→Formatter bridge**: `messageCommand` parsed `--limit` and passed it to the provider, but never forwarded it to the formatter.
3. **Pagination visibility**: Providers (Slack/Matrix/MS Teams) already returned pagination metadata, but the CLI renderer never surfaced it.

This is a minimal fix — no heuristic hints, no return-value signature changes, no new abstractions.

### Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/commands/message-format.ts` | `FormatOpts` gains `displayLimit`; `renderMessageList` uses it (default 25); new `renderPaginationHint` emits one muted line when provider cursor signals exist (`hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`); `formatMessageCliText` accepts optional `displayLimit` param; search branch checks payload → nested results → `total_results > returned_count` to cover Discord's three pagination-signal shapes |
| `src/commands/message.ts` | Parses `--limit` via `parsePositiveIntOrUndefined` and forwards it to `formatMessageCliText` |
| `src/commands/message-format.test.ts` (new) | 12 tests: displayLimit honored for read/pins/search, default 25, below-limit rendering, pagination hints for `hasMore` / `nextBatch` / `@odata.nextLink`, nested-results `hasMore`, `total_results` exceeding vs equaling returned count, no false hint |

## Why This Approach (vs #79593)

#79593 is the prior art (~400 LOC, CONFLICTING, unmaintained since May). This PR keeps the same core fix (displayLimit threading) while dropping the three controversial pieces:

- **No "Showing X of Y" truncation hint** — requires changing `renderMessageList`'s return signature
- **No "Reached --limit (N)" heuristic** — unreliable when the provider returned exactly the requested count (Discord has no `hasMore`)
- **No CHANGELOG.md edit** — release-owned file

## Evidence

- Tests: 12 formatter tests + 6 message tests, all passing
- oxlint: clean
- oxfmt: clean
- Live Matrix verification with `nextBatch`:

```
$ node openclaw.mjs message read --target '!room:server' --channel matrix

Messages
┌──────────────────┬──────────────┬──────────┬──────────┐
│ ...              │ ...          │ ...      │ ...      │
└──────────────────┴──────────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
More results available. Use --limit to fetch more, or --json for the raw cursor.
```

## User Impact

- **Before**: `openclaw message read --limit 50` rendered only 25 rows with no indication more existed. Provider pagination cursors (Matrix `nextBatch`, Slack `hasMore`, MS Teams `@odata.nextLink`) were invisible to CLI users. Discord search with `total_results` gave no hint of remaining matches.
- **After**: `--limit` is honored — `--limit 50` renders up to 50 rows. When the provider signals more results are available (any of `hasMore`, `nextBatch`, or `@odata.nextLink`), a muted hint line appears below the table. Discord search additionally checks nested `hasMore` and `total_results > returned_count` so completed searches do not show a false hint.
- **Default behavior unchanged**: omitting `--limit` still defaults to 25 rows.
- **JSON output unchanged**: `--json` continues to carry raw provider payloads including cursor fields.
